title: What the rerun must run
prompt: The starter defines the platform's seven nightly tasks. Three of them raise an error when the data is wrong, and after tonight's run the team fixed a bug in `dim_accounts`. Finish `solve` so it runs the night and returns one row per task: its name in `task`, its `status`, and in `rerun` whether tomorrow's rerun must run it.
rules: `failed`: the task ran and raised an error. `skipped`: a task it needs is `failed` or `skipped`, so it didn't run. `ok`: it ran without an error. Tasks that don't need a failed task still run.

The rerun must run every task that isn't `ok`. Because its code changed, it must also run `dim_accounts` and every task that needs it, directly or through other tasks. Every other task keeps tonight's output.
Return all seven tasks. `rerun` is a boolean.
hints: First the statuses, as in lesson 77: walk `run_order(deps)` and look at the statuses of the tasks each one needs before running it.
A task's output changes when the code of a task it needs changes. Walking the run order once finds everything below `dim_accounts`.
`rerun` is true when the status isn't `ok`, or when the task is `dim_accounts` or below it.
